steps.text: 17 Years Ago
3:09 P.M. \ Clear
Ursus, 147km northwest from the main course of nomadic city Chernobog, village
A hamlet...

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Quick, quick, the doctor says to get warm water!

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Where would we find warm water so easily? Ask Marfa, ask if her family still has any water they boiled this morning.

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Emperor above, we beg you, bless our old dedushka...
Excuse me... What's happening here; who's the doctor you mentioned?

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Oh, you're... who are you?

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Where did you come from... your clothes mean you're from the city, right? Sorry, sorry, we're busy aiding someone right now... If you don't mind, come with me this way, at least you'll have a place to sit.
It's okay... I came here to find that doctor, as it happens. What's her name?

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: You... you're not here to...
She's just a shady doctor. Do you have great trust in her?

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: But she... she's all we have who can save our dedushka. I beg you, I'm begging you, at least just for now—she's only a doctor here to save us.
I'm not here to seize her. I just have a little business with her.
Could you show me the way?

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: I... I don't know if...
I'm a doctor too. Perhaps I can be of help.

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Oh, even a burdenbeast would know you're a scholar, seeing your clothes...
You can tell Dr. Kal'tsit something first. Tell her, her student Lillia's here to visit her, and ask her if she needs any assistance or not.

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Ah, so you know the doctor's name, and you're Lillia, is that right? Good, good, truly a wonderful name. Wait there for a moment, I'll go right now.

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Ay, hey! Don't forget to ask Marfa, bring warm water over!

steps.name: Patient
steps.text: Ugh, ughah...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Grit your teeth, and keep holding on.

steps.name: Patient
steps.text: Ugheaaagh—grh—

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: ...Kal'tsit...

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: What's going on here?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Attacked by a wild beast. This is just emergency treatment.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Knife.

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Ah, er... where—where was it... I can't find...

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Here. Hand.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: An Infected creature?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Any risk of Infection?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Most Infected creatures are cleaner than people imagine. By the toothmarks, a tuskbeast roaming the vicinity.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: But if it's come into contact with active Originium...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Infected creatures may have methods to coexist with pathogens, but humans do not.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The situation is severe. This is not Originium infection alone. Additional necrosis symptoms are present.

steps.name: Patient
steps.text: Hurts... so much...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Calm down, now. Deep breaths.

steps.name: Patient
steps.text: Hphhh—haaah—hphhh—

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Difficulty breathing, likely thrombosis. All symptomatic of acute Oripathy.

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: But—But doesn't Oripathy make crystals grow out of your skin?! Our dedushka's fine, see, isn't he?!

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: In certain circumstances, the source of infection ends up rapidly circulating through the blood, and won't present visible Originium crystals like regular cases of Oripathy do. Infection symptoms intensify within a short time, very quickly.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: If we don't suppress it via drugs... mm.

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Emperor above, Emperor above...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You've learned a lot.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Syringes are... inside the gray medical kit.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Here... You carried a suppressant like this with you?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There's always times of need.

steps.name: Patient
steps.text: Wait... *cough* *cough* Do—Doctor... is this—expensive?

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Thinking about that at a time like this?!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's affordable. You have no need to worry. Our top priority right now is suppressing your acute Oripathic responses, and prevent an Originium crystal dust outburst.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You don't want the others in the village to suffer because of you, correct?

steps.name: Patient
steps.text: Ugh!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Steady breaths. Relax.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You'll be fine.

steps.name: Patient
steps.text: Ngh, alright...

steps.name: Patient
steps.text: Hfff—haaah—

steps.name: Patient
steps.text: Urgh... hff... do—doctor... I don't want to... become Inf... *cough* *cough*... Infected...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm very sorry.

steps.name: Patient
steps.text: I... *sob*... I... *cough* *cough*... *cough* *hack* *cough*...

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Suffocation. We don't have a respirator...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We have nothing here, but that doesn't mean we can do nothing. Bring the inhaler over.

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Doctor! Doctor! I'm begging you, save this dedushka of ours, damn it!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The moment Originium dust permeated his wounds, it was inevitable he'd become an Infected, and all I can do is strive to extend his life.

steps.name: Patient
steps.text: Hck, *cough*, *hack* *cough* *cough*—huff, hahh—

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Has the suppressant still not taken effect?!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Considering the patient's age, the suppressant itself was a tremendous risk. Hold your nerve.

steps.name: Patient
steps.text: ...hah... hah...

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Breathing has stabilized some...

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Is he better now? Is his sickness gone?

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: In terms of his acute symptoms, possibly. But if you mean his Oripathy, we can do nothing. No one can do anything.

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: How could this... Then if the man from the Patrol Unit comes by...

steps.name: Patient
steps.text: Then just—Then just give me... give me up! I only had so long left anyway... Infected? Fine, so be it... Just as long as you don't let the eggheads in here to run their mouths...

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: No! We wouldn't, we wouldn't, we just have to hide you. We won't let anyone find you. We'll all hide you safely.

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Doctor, thank you so much, doctor, things might not have turned out best, but we... well, we don't have much to repay you with either...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This is merely a doctor's duty. The path ahead of becoming an Infected... is what you truly need to consider. I'm very sorry, that circumstances couldn't permit me to do more.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Suppressant is effective, but wounds are still infected. It may lead to worsening of thrombosis... We may have to operate and excise...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your judgment is correct. Good sir. Please bear with this.

steps.name: Patient
steps.text: Agh—alright... alright... eaaargh, ungh—!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Sorry about that, Lillia.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Long time no see, Director Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Long time no see. Let's walk and talk.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Perhaps... you're not enthused about conversing with me like this after that bloodbath, but from the bottom of my heart, I'm glad you're still alive.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: So after that, you hid here the whole time?

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: From the hill over there, you can see out to Chernobog's skyscrapers. If it were me, I wouldn't opt to shelter so near a cityway.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm only stopping over for the moment, nothing more.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: What... What have you been doing, ever since?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I don't wish for the hate between you to continue flowing unabated. In particular, it's a hatred that will not only cause one to find their own ruin, but will strongly attract direct reprisal from those murderers.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: You're telling me all this on purpose, aren't you?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I won't deny that, Lillia. But...

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit, you're leaving?

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Ah, it's...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: My student. No alarm, she came to pick me up.

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Ah, I see, then... But, well, pick you up?

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Oh, Emperor above... You're going after all then?

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: If you're going, please tell us! You cured my daughter, so at least let us send you off properly!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I will.

steps.name: Ursus Villager
steps.text: Ah, alright, alright, then we'll leave you two alone. You have to tell us before you go, please, Dr. Kal'tsit... don't forget.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: The people here seem to like you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They've shown enough goodwill already. I've merely done my work as a doctor.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: They're the ones who live true Ursus lives. We've spent so long in the Research Institute, there's plenty we've forgotten.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Even positioning themselves near a cityway couldn't bring them opportunity, nor prosperity.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Precisely the opposite. A tyrant official with subordinate power took hold there, exploiting the poor folk to offer the Patrol Unit yet more convenient soil.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: So they can't even find one run-of-the-mill doctor graduated from medical school. And one run-of-the-mill flu strain could kill a tender young girl.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Your horizons are vast. Yes, they've always been... You'd still treat a flu for someone? I thought...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You thought I was a scientist who gesticulated at papers and data.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: To be honest, you're more a doctor than I even imagined.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Perhaps I always was a doctor. What changes is only the treatment subject and the locus to contend with.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: It's why your students put so much faith in you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Lillia.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: How's your daughter?

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: I left her with a friend of mine. She has no connection to all this whatsoever.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: You know... how young she is. She doesn't even speak yet. She hasn't begun to walk...

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: And I left behind my child just like that.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You could've chosen not to do this. If you wanted Louisa to live on, identity concealed—

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: You should know what I think, Director Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I just want to try and stop you. But if not even your daughter can stall your step, perhaps my words won't reach you either.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: That's right. I'm quite clear about that.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Winter's so cold this year.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Vampilov's father went mad from his son's death. He kept fowlbeasts penned in a loft by the lake, and every day would fantasize for a while he was going hunting with his son.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Ilia's child, Lyudmila, she's still young, but already comprehends certain, irreversible things. Nobody even knows how she's doing nowadays.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: And Romanovich, too. His family sold off their whole estate, and left that city. Even if his brothers never believed in any accident, there were people to shut them up.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: And for even more. The police announced it was an accident down to the finest thing.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: In that 'list of accidental casualties,' not a single person had left Chernobog's research institute. An experimental accident leading to a chain reaction, and reported identities of bodies provided by the military.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: But a kind of intuition tells me... some are alive.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Intuition?

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Because afterwards, all relatives of the victims, more or less, received anonymous aid—as well as a warning.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: I don't think that spineless, incompetent Marquess Boris, nor Sergei, that traitor, would have any mercy in them. So, someone else who knows what happened has to have survived.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: But it took until today, three years later, before I found you, Director Kal'tsit. It took until today. You hid so well, you even fooled the Secret Police's eyes...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They rely too much on Ursus's latest technology for criminal investigation. It actually created an opening for me.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Of course... you're a hailed genius. An incomparable research leader. That's why everyone embraces you so.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: —Please tell me, Lillia. How many people signed on to your plan?

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Six or seven. Maybe even more; we don't dare meet together in public. We might be caught, used for leverage.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: That includes me. All lost things in that 'accident' they can never have back.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: When did you start plotting all of this?

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: From the moment I found out the Fourth Army's lackeys fired the first bolt in the Research Institute, mercilessly shredding the father of my children's throat. From that moment, I started.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Lillia...

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Don't take me as a brave fool. Even if my health gives me so little time to work with you all... I've still accomplished one thing or another. Such as—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You found the whereabouts of Grand Duke Vanya. The Pine Valley Retreat, situated beyond any nomadic city.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And this former Fourth Army staff officer was also highly likely to be a Grand Duke of Ursus actualizing the Sarcophagus incident, perhaps right in the frailest, weakest position of his endlessly long campaign career.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You want to conduct an assassination, Lillia, but this act of vengeance can still be considered 'bravely foolish.'

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: ...Heh.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: I can finally see why my husband... why that Astrov looked up to you so.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But you must know, Lillia, assassinating an old Grand Duke will have no significance at all.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Maybe from the start, Vanya, the man so decrepit he needs cardiac stimulant injections when he gives speeches, was not the real murderer.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: I know, Kal'tsit, I know...

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: But do you really think when I entrusted Louisa to someone else, it was just for a rational ending, a so-called fair trial? As if you can't guess, Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Blind revenge will only cause you to lack foresight.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Kal'tsit, Kal'tsit. Perhaps you couldn't understand.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Louisa never even learned to say 'papa.'

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You can sit.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: How long have you spent in here?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Not worth mentioning. Lillia. You look awful. You need to rest.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: How did you find me?

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Just sheer chance... if not for sheer chance, perhaps I'd have never learned you were still alive.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Lyudmila.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: We didn't want our children coming to too much harm, so at first, we planned to look for Lyudmila.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: But then, we learned from Lyudmila's housekeeper that someone was sustaining contact with them, aiding them. Someone anonymous, but she seemed to know it all, inside and out.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: The same anonym had even set up a way for her to leave Ursus.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: It was then I was sure that some were still alive. And to my knowledge, very few could accomplish something like that.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Have some tea.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Here I imagined you'd be itching to ask about my business at the Retreat.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Lillia, I imagine the one who's really itching here is you.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: And you knew all along exactly where Vanya was... you're really just going to sit on the sidelines? You should know all the secrets he's holding onto!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The true secrets have already been sealed for eternity in that research institute, thanks to Ilia's perseverance. Even now, the Army haven't been able to find a single scrap of the gains they were drooling for.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And Grand Duke Vanya is incurably ill. He'll recuperate at Pine Valley every winter. Provided you have any way to sneak into a so-called high-class salon even once, it's not hard to come by the information.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: He even brags all over about how the retreat is so beautiful and vast.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Correct. There is no shortage of Ursus soldiers with outstanding service there, and of course, bureaucrats and nobles too.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Infiltrating it and assassinating a Grand Duke would be as absurd as you, in Chernobog, charging into Marquess Boris's house with a knife, slitting his throat open and then escaping again untouched.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: You're right. But for those 'bureaucrats and nobles,' security in there is still weak enough to make people restless.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I won't deny that. But how do you know that's not a signal, one that Grand Duke Vanya is no longer an important figure, or that...

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Or that his fate has already been set by certain people? I've told you, Kal'tsit, what I want isn't a fair trial. To make it clear, what I long for is a lynching.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Now's not the time to discuss justice or morality, Kal'tsit. Only those who can rest easy at night enjoy using 'objectivity' as a shield.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Whether Grand Duke Vanya is censured by the military or the Emperor, becomes a scapegoat, stands the wrong side in political conflict, suffers banishment, is stowed away by the Army...

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: —No matter what, even if he dies miserably in the end at the gallows, what business is that of mine?

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: It was him who pushed for all of Chernobog to sink into deeper ruin, and all I know is he should pay the price. He should pay the price to us! He's the murderer who killed my child's father!

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Kal'tsit!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm listening...

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: I've already figured out how to infiltrate the retreat... but I also need to admit, even if the security there is suspiciously weak, that doesn't mean any of us can pull this off smoothly.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: I've found a breach. Someone who's been in charge of security at that noble's sanatorium for thirty-plus years, but hasn't had the guts to make much side-money off it for fear of the nobles.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: I... prepared a huge sum, with my colleagues' help. That complete life failure, who we all saw could retire any day, caved in instantly.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: We spent immense effort to gain his trust. I was simply the daughter of a country upstart, only wanting to intern at the retreat to get close with some noble or officer.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You want me to help you.

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: Yes. Forging any identity has risks no matter what, but to my mind, the retreat and the information agency wouldn't be that tied up, so—

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: If even the Secret Police are fooled into thinking you're dead—

steps.name: Lillia
steps.text: —then death will be your open road.

a.text: In 1080, the Sarcophagus Incident's surviving scientist, Sergei, established a brand-new research institute.
The same year, Marquess Boris vastly expanded Chernobog's industrial region. The Fourth Army's Messengers, for the first time in history, found the Marquess's door was closed to them there.
Lyudmila was still young, and Louisa was but one amongst countless children, so Kal'tsit thought. She could comprehend that Lillia, as a mother, had complex, cruel expectations of these children.
And after the Chernobog Core City's engine underwent its umpteenth major maintenance, it still turned with a rumble.
